newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Cautious, tight-ranged trade seen on Seoul bourse.
newsitem.headline: Cautious, tight-ranged trade seen on Seoul bourse.

text.p: Stocks are forecast to move in a narrow range on Tuesday on persistent jitters about financial troubles at Jinro, brokers said.
Expectations of strong selling pressure at around the 700 level would also keep investors cautious, they said.
"Slow trading is likely. Many investors appear to think the market needs a further consolidation before a major rally begins," said a Daewoo Securities broker.
On Monday the composite index fell 3.31 points to 697.34.
The recent financial trouble at the Jinro Group highlighted a hardship facing many other shaky companies, brokers said.
Jinro, the nation's 19th largest conglomerate, said last week it was selling off some of its property and affiliates to raise cash for debt repayments. Its debts are valued at about 3.2 trillion won.

On Monday Jinro's prime lender, the Commercial Bank of Korea, said it would bail out six of Jinro's 24 units according to an earlier agreement with other financial institutions to prevent more companies from folding.
